headline: Curry scores 41 as Warriors win seventh straight in OT

top.headline: Curry scores 41 as Warriors win seventh straight in OT
top.summary: Stephen Curry had 41 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists in a 126-119 overtime win in Orlando, scoring 12 in the last 2:21 of regulation before Jamal Cain's tip-in forced OT. It's his 16th 40-point game since turning 35, passing LeBron James (15) and Michael Jordan (12). Per ESPN, the 7-3 Warriors are only the second team to follow an 0-3 start with seven straight wins, after the 1950-51 Celtics.

top.headline: McDavid stretches season-opening point streak to 18
top.summary: Connor McDavid had three assists and Leon Draisaitl scored twice in a 4-2 win over Vancouver. NHL.com says 18 straight games to open a season is the longest by an active player, passing McDavid's own 17 from 2021-22. He leads the league with 47 points and is two games short of his career-best 20. The Canucks are 1-14-1 in their last 16.

top.headline: Colts open for business on Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor
top.summary: Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter report the Colts are listening to offers for QB Daniel Jones and RB Jonathan Taylor ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline. The Ravens reportedly called about Jones before trading for Jacoby Brissett. Schefter also says Derrick Henry is expected to stay in Baltimore.

The Ravens reportedly called about Jones before trading for Jacoby Brissett. Schefter also says Derrick Henry is expected to stay in Baltimore.

stories.headline: Broncos ask about Trey McBride, Cardinals say no
stories.summary: Per ESPN, Denver checked in on Arizona TE Trey McBride, who leads the NFL with 66 catches, and was turned down. The Broncos want an upgrade over Evan Engram (13 catches, 136 yards, 1 TD) before Tuesday.

stories.headline: Jaguars shop for defense; Brian Thomas Jr. draws calls
stories.summary: Jacksonville has been calling around for a defensive playmaker after losing NT DaVon Hamilton and S Eric Murray for the season, per Schefter and Rapoport. The Jaguars have had "multiple inquiries" about WR Brian Thomas Jr., who could be part of a deal.

stories.headline: Aiyuk saga: 'To be continued'
stories.summary: Friday's meeting at the 49ers' offices didn't end in a reinstatement. A dispute over roughly $13 million in forfeited bonus money now involves the NFL Management Council and the NFLPA, and San Francisco still holds his rights. Agent Drew Rosenhaus: "To be continued."

stories.headline: Lions lose Jack Campbell to IR; Saints get Tyson and Banks back
stories.summary: Detroit put LB Jack Campbell on IR, so he's out at least four games after being taken off on a backboard against Minnesota. New Orleans' No. 8 pick Jordyn Tyson is set to debut off IR against Cleveland, with LT Kelvin Banks Jr. expected back for the first time since Week 2. Deshaun Watson cleared concussion protocol, but Shedeur Sanders still starts.

leagues.summary: Curry's 41 extends Golden State's streak to seven; Spurs win eight straight; Thunder hold Washington to 75

It's his 16th 40-point game since turning 35, passing LeBron James (15) and Michael Jordan (12). Per ESPN, the 7-3 Warriors are only the second team to follow an 0-3 start with seven straight wins, after the 1950-51 Celtics.

stories.headline: Spurs win eighth straight, sit starters for the fourth
stories.summary: San Antonio won 125-103 in Portland. Victor Wembanyama scored 29 in 24 minutes on 9-of-13 shooting, and the starters sat the fourth with a 33-point lead. At 8-2, it's the Spurs' longest streak since 11 straight last March.

stories.headline: Thunder hold Wizards to 75, the NBA's lowest total this season
stories.summary: Oklahoma City won 114-75 as Washington shot 29 of 98, including 7 of 43 from three. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 30 in three quarters. OKC is 8-2 with Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren out long-term, per AP.

stories.headline: Booker's late burst gets Suns past Houston
stories.summary: Devin Booker scored seven straight to break a 95-all tie in a 102-99 win, and Kevin Durant missed a potential tying 3 at the end. It's Phoenix's first set of back-to-back wins this season.

stories.headline: Nuggets beat Haliburton-less Pacers in Mexico City
stories.summary: Denver won 114-102 at Arena CDMX behind Nikola Jokic's 19 points, 13 rebounds and 8 assists. Indiana, without Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring), has lost five of six and is 3-7.

standouts.note: Scored 12 in the last 2:21 of regulation to force OT.

leagues.summary: McDavid's point streak hits 18; Jack Hughes wins it in OT; Stamkos passes Robitaille; Canes score nine

stories.summary: Connor McDavid had three assists and Leon Draisaitl scored twice in a 4-2 win over Vancouver. NHL.com says 18 straight games to open a season is the longest by an active player, passing McDavid's own 17 from 2021-22. He leads the league with 47 points and is two games short of his career-best 20. The Canucks are 1-14-1 in their last 16.

stories.headline: Jack Hughes ends Devils' comeback in OT on Long Island
stories.summary: New Jersey trailed by two in the third, tied it on Dougie Hamilton's power-play goal and won 5-4 on Hughes' breakaway 1:18 into overtime. It's his league-leading third OT goal, and the 12-5-0 Devils have won four straight. Ilya Sorokin made 45 saves in the loss.

stories.headline: Stamkos moves to fifth all-time in power-play goals
stories.summary: Steven Stamkos scored his 248th career power-play goal, passing Luc Robitaille, in Nashville's 3-1 win over St. Louis. The Predators have won four straight; the Blues have lost three in a row.

stories.headline: Hurricanes score nine before flying to Finland
stories.summary: Carolina beat Chicago 9-2, with two goals each from Jordan Martinook and Andrei Svechnikov. The 14-3-2 Hurricanes head to Helsinki to play Seattle on Nov. 12 and 14. Chicago has lost six straight.

stories.headline: Canadiens win in Toronto, point streak hits 10
stories.summary: Alex Newhook scored twice and Jacob Fowler made 26 saves in a 4-2 win. Montreal is 8-0-2 in its last 10; the Leafs have lost four of five and lost Morgan Rielly to a lower-body injury.

standouts.name: Martin Necas
standouts.note: Both goals came on the power play in a 4-0 win over Detroit.

standouts.name: Connor McDavid
standouts.note: Point streak to open the season is now 18.

standouts.name: Mackenzie Blackwood
standouts.note: His first shutout of the season.

stories.headline: Skubal is the unanimous No. 1 free-agent starter
stories.summary: MLB.com's free-agent starting pitcher rankings put Tarik Skubal first by unanimous vote, ahead of Michael King, Freddy Peralta, Sonny Gray and NPB's Kaima Taira. Skubal missed about six weeks with an elbow injury this year and still tops the board.
